rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi reads the instruction as forbidding believers to remain where revelation is rejected or mocked until the discussion changes.
rows.anchor: wherever you hear that God’s revelations are being rejected and ridiculed, do not sit there with them until they get engaged in some other talk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the singular address appears directed to the Prophet, it reaches all believers through him; the next verse and 4:140 establish its general scope.
rows.anchor: in reality it is directed to all the believers through him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preaching to opponents in a frenzy only intensifies their agitation, so Muslims should wait until they return to normal before presenting Islam.
rows.anchor: presenting that very thing before him in this condition will only enhance his frenzy and hysteria

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remaining silent when someone openly speaks nonsense against God and the Messenger is incompatible with a preacher’s honour and support for truth.
rows.anchor: not only fighting with him is wrong for a preacher, but also remaining silent for him is inapt

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defending truth is a sign of faith; tolerating humiliation of God, the Messenger, Qur’an, and sharia can gradually lead to hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: This weakness of faith can ultimately lead a person in a gradual way to hypocrisy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to al-Nisāʾ explains the honour aspect: hypocrites were reprimanded for joining gatherings where revelation was mocked despite being forbidden to do so.
rows.anchor: the hypocrites are reprimanded for participating in the gatherings of the rivals where God’s revelations were openly made fun of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When conversation turns to mockery, believers should leave even if they fear rivals will ridicule them for abandoning a polemical debate.
rows.anchor: if he now leaves that place his rivals will ridicule him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Staying out of deference to a gathering shows lost religious honour; one would not stay silent if parents were abused, while duty to God is greater.
rows.anchor: the obligation he owes to God and His directives is much greater than his obligation to his parents

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing a debate to prove truth becomes ego when corrupted minds will only grow angrier; it harms truth, so the believer should recognize Satan’s ploy and leave.
rows.anchor: such an engagement merely becomes a question of one’s ego. It will not be helpful for the cause of truth at all

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan tricks believers into such a gathering, they should leave as soon as they recognize their mistake, while remaining vigilant against deception.
rows.anchor: they should leave the gathering as soon as they realize their folly

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mockers of God’s revelations are especially unjust to themselves, and believers cannot know when God may punish hypocrites for keeping their company.
rows.anchor: those who make fun of God’s revelations are the ones who are the most unjust to their souls

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance that God-fearing believers are not accountable for opponents calls for wise, moderate preaching: convey God’s religion so they may fear Him.
rows.anchor: the responsibility of the believers regarding the disbelievers is to merely communicate the religion of God to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are not responsible for forcing conversion; acceptance is rewarded, while persistent disbelief is the disbeliever’s responsibility before God on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: The believers are not responsible for changing the faith of the disbelievers by force

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul answers for another; the believer’s duty is to convey and remind, waiting for a suitable moment rather than pursuing people to make them believe.
rows.anchor: before God no soul will be responsible for another

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi links the assurance to 5:105: those who remain rightly guided cannot be harmed by people who stray.
rows.anchor: if you are on the right path, then those who have strayed cannot harm you at all

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse gradually clarifies that the previous verse’s singular address is directed to the believers generally.
rows.anchor: though in the previous verse the address was singular, but the discourse was directed at the believers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses reveal the Companions’ zeal to bear witness to truth: they thought they would be liable if people failed to accept faith.
rows.anchor: they thought that if people did not accept faith they would be held liable for it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses stress preaching: believers are not liable for others’ refusal to believe, but are liable if they fail to preach and remind them.
rows.anchor: they will certainly be held reliable if they did not preach and remind people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion means the faith God revealed and that the Prophet and his Companions presented to the people.
rows.anchor: religion God revealed to them and which the prophet and his companions were presenting to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should leave mockers alone rather than pursue or appease people who treat life carelessly and religion as amusement.
rows.anchor: there is no need to satisfy people who are non-serious and careless about life

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mockers infer from worldly success that their conduct is right, but this life is a test where evil too receives respite; they treat worldly desires as religion and dismiss the Qur’an’s warning of the hereafter.
rows.anchor: This world is not governed by the principle of reward and punishment; on the contrary, it is governed by the principle of trial and test

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the warning about a soul being consigned refers back to the Qur’an mentioned in 6:68.
rows.anchor: mentioned earlier in verse 68

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi explains absala as being consigned to death and the related expression as being consigned to one’s deeds.
rows.anchor: he was consigned to death

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the particle an, a governing noun meaning fear is omitted according to linguistic principles.
rows.anchor: a governing noun to the effect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible rendering is to warn through the Qur’an lest a soul be consigned to death because of its deeds.
rows.anchor: lest a soul is consigned to death because of its deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second rendering warns lest a soul be consigned to its deeds or held in ransom because of them.
rows.anchor: a soul is consigned to its deeds or is held in

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the two renderings do not differ substantially in meaning.
rows.anchor: There is not much difference in both these translations in essence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet need not chase mockers or answer their changing demands; he must remind them through the Qur’an that everyone will face deeds that save or destroy them.
rows.anchor: He should only discharge his responsibility of reminding them through the Qur’ ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is that no helper, supporter, intercessor, or accepted ransom will rescue a person in the hereafter; after warning, disbelief is the person’s own responsibility and the Prophet is acquitted.
rows.anchor: None will be there to help or support or intercessor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who ignore the warning are consigned to their deeds and face boiling water and painful torment; boiling water is their first hospitality, as also described in al-Wāqiʿah.
rows.anchor: is mentioned as their first hospitality

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers will wish to ransom their children, spouse, brothers, and family to escape torment, but cannot fulfill that wish.
rows.anchor: the wrongdoers will desire to be able to give their children, their wife, their brothers and their family in ransom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ensuing verses imply that people might once have had an excuse for error, but after the Prophet’s guidance they have none.
rows.anchor: if these people were in error earlier on, they had an excuse. But now that the Prophet’s guidance had come to them, what excuse will they have

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle mā humiliates the deities; denial of their benefit or harm concerns their essence, since any effect occurs by God’s directive.
rows.anchor: signifies humiliation for their deities and the negation of benefit or harm relates to its essence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder of guidance warns those who stumble and mislead others after clear guidance to reflect on their fate.
rows.anchor: those who stumble and make others stumble even after this clear guidance has come to them should reflect on their fate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istahwāʾ means to make someone lose their senses and become bewildered.
rows.anchor: to make someone lose his senses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-arḍ generally means land, but the desert is intended here because the parable concerns wandering where one may go astray.
rows.anchor: there is danger for a person to go astray

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the verb to devils reflects the parable’s meaning: devils among jinn and humans cause losses of faith and morality, so the attribution points to reality.
rows.anchor: Devils among jinn and mankind are mostly responsible for it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudā also means the straight path.
rows.anchor: The word  ﻫﺪى also means “the straight path.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable explains being turned back after guidance: a person led astray by devils in a desert wanders confused while companions call him to the path, but he cannot find his way.
rows.anchor: he is then called by his companions to the straight path but he has been left bereft of his intellect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the parable’s wording seems general, Islahi applies it to Islam’s opponents, lost like travelers through devils and misguided leaders while believing compatriots call them to truth.
rows.anchor: they are like travellers who have lost their way in a desert

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene is beautifully drawn: it appears to describe others, but in reality describes the opponents under discussion.
rows.anchor: The parable apparently relates to others; however, in reality, it relates to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration of submission answers the polytheists’ invitation: believers are called to worship the Lord of the worlds, not things unable to benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: these people are inviting the believers to worship those things which can neither harm nor benefit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words to Him emphasize God’s command, while Lord of the worlds gives the reason: only the world’s Lord is worthy of submission.
rows.anchor: if God is the Lord of the worlds, who else can be worthy of being submitted to

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to establish prayer and fear God until the gathering is governed by submission and portrays it in practice.
rows.anchor: are governed by the submission just mentioned and are actually its practical portrayal
